title: The Magnet in the Nose
own_credit: Akron and Lakewood photographs by Matthew Hagan

lines.speaker: TITLE
lines.visual: card:Akron, Ohio|The Magnet in the Nose

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Akron, Ohio. The Rubber City. Every summer since the nineteen thirties, kids have come here to roll down a hill in cars they built themselves. No engine. Just gravity. And in 1973, gravity got some help.
lines.caption: Akron, Ohio. The Rubber City. Every summer since the nineteen thirties, kids have come here to roll down a hill in cars they built themselves. No engine. Just gravity. And in 1973, gravity got some help.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: I know a little about this. Eighth grade science, Mr. Kobalt's class. We ran a mini pinewood derby. My takeaways were, aerodynamics be darned. Pack that thing with mass and keep the wheels lubed. That is the whole science of a gravity race. There is no step three.
lines.caption: I know a little about this. Eighth grade science, Mr. Kobalt's class. We ran a mini pinewood derby. My takeaways were, aerodynamics be darned. Pack that thing with mass and keep the wheels lubed. That is the whole science of a gravity race. There is no step three.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Oh, I know this one. Kid from Colorado stuck a magnet in his car. Cheated, got caught, went home. That is the whole story.
lines.caption: Oh, I know this one. Kid from Colorado stuck a magnet in his car. Cheated, got caught, went home. That is the whole story.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Nick, that is the first ten seconds of the story.
lines.caption: Nick, that is the first ten seconds of the story.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: August 19, 1973. Derby Downs. A hundred and thirty-eight racers, eleven to fifteen years old. The winner is Jimmy Gronen, fourteen, from Boulder, Colorado.
lines.caption: August 19, 1973. Derby Downs. A hundred and thirty-eight racers, eleven to fifteen years old. The winner is Jimmy Gronen, fourteen, from Boulder, Colorado.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: And people in the stands noticed something. When the steel starting gate dropped, his car seemed to jump.
lines.caption: And people in the stands noticed something. When the steel starting gate dropped, his car seemed to jump.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Here is how it worked. An electromagnet in the nose of the car. A battery in the tail. And a switch behind his head. He leans his helmet back, the magnet grabs the steel starting gate, and when the gate falls forward it pulls the car with it.
lines.caption: Here is how it worked. An electromagnet in the nose of the car. A battery in the tail. And a switch behind his head. He leans his helmet back, the magnet grabs the steel starting gate, and when the gate falls forward it pulls the car with it.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: That is actually pretty slick. For a fourteen-year-old.
lines.caption: That is actually pretty slick. For a fourteen-year-old.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And that is the tell, Nick. A fourteen-year-old did not do that.
lines.caption: And that is the tell, Nick. A fourteen-year-old did not do that.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Officials X-rayed the car. Two days after the race, they took the title away.
lines.caption: Officials X-rayed the car. Two days after the race, they took the title away.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The car was built under the eye of his uncle and legal guardian, Robert Lange. Lange made his fortune in ski boots. The rules said a kid builds his own car and spends no more than seventy-five dollars. Lange reportedly spent about twenty-two thousand.
lines.caption: The car was built under the eye of his uncle and legal guardian, Robert Lange. Lange made his fortune in ski boots. The rules said a kid builds his own car and spends no more than seventy-five dollars. Lange reportedly spent about twenty-two thousand.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Twenty-two thousand dollars. On a soap box.
lines.caption: Twenty-two thousand dollars. On a soap box.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Then the uncle wrote a letter to the Derby. He said the magnet trick had been around for years. He said the rules were consistently and notoriously violated. And he said it was common knowledge that no eleven-year-old could build a car that wins.
lines.caption: Then the uncle wrote a letter to the Derby. He said the magnet trick had been around for years. He said the rules were consistently and notoriously violated. And he said it was common knowledge that no eleven-year-old could build a car that wins.
lines.visual: card:“Consistently and notoriously violated”|Robert Lange's letter to the Derby · TIME, September 10, 1973

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: And he was not wrong about that part. Investigators later found at least thirty Derby cars with illegal axles.
lines.caption: And he was not wrong about that part. Investigators later found at least thirty Derby cars with illegal axles.
lines.visual: card:At least 30 cars|found with illegal axles

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: So the whole hill was dirty.
lines.caption: So the whole hill was dirty.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The whole hill was grown-ups. Engineers. Dads with machine shops. Professional builders. The kids were the drivers, and the kids were the cover story.
lines.caption: The whole hill was grown-ups. Engineers. Dads with machine shops. Professional builders. The kids were the drivers, and the kids were the cover story.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And look who built the stage. For almost forty years the Derby belonged to Chevrolet. General Motors put a boy and a Chevy bowtie in every newspaper in America. Then in 1972 they decided it was not worth the money, and they walked.
lines.caption: And look who built the stage. For almost forty years the Derby belonged to Chevrolet. General Motors put a boy and a Chevy bowtie in every newspaper in America. Then in 1972 they decided it was not worth the money, and they walked.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Akron was left holding the hill. The Chamber of Commerce ran it in seventy-three. After the magnet, they walked too.
lines.caption: Akron was left holding the hill. The Chamber of Commerce ran it in seventy-three. After the magnet, they walked too.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The county prosecutor here said it was like seeing apple pie, motherhood and the American flag grinding to a halt.
lines.caption: The county prosecutor here said it was like seeing apple pie, motherhood and the American flag grinding to a halt.
lines.visual: card:“Apple pie, motherhood and the American flag”|The Summit County prosecutor, 1973

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: Come on. It is a magnet in a gravity car.
lines.caption: Come on. It is a magnet in a gravity car.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: That is my point, Nick. So count up who paid. The uncle gave two thousand dollars to a boys' club, said he was sorry, and sat out two years. General Motors was already gone.
lines.caption: That is my point, Nick. So count up who paid. The uncle gave two thousand dollars to a boys' club, said he was sorry, and sat out two years. General Motors was already gone.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: And the fourteen-year-old lost the title, lost a seventy-five hundred dollar scholarship, and got his name in every paper in the country next to the word cheater.
lines.caption: And the fourteen-year-old lost the title, lost a seventy-five hundred dollar scholarship, and got his name in every paper in the country next to the word cheater.

lines.speaker: R
lines.say: Years later he said one thing about it. The derby was corrupt before we arrived.
lines.caption: Years later he said one thing about it. The derby was corrupt before we arrived.
lines.visual: card:“The derby was corrupt before we arrived.”|Jimmy Gronen, years later

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The family of the boy who was handed the trophy said, I feel terrible for the kid. That is more grace than any grown-up on that hill showed all summer.
lines.caption: The family of the boy who was handed the trophy said, I feel terrible for the kid. That is more grace than any grown-up on that hill showed all summer.

lines.speaker: S
lines.say: All right. I take it back. The kid drove the car. Somebody else built the lie.
lines.caption: All right. I take it back. The kid drove the car. Somebody else built the lie.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: A grown man spends twenty-two thousand dollars to win a children's race. A car company uses children to sell cars and leaves when the bill comes. And the only one whose name gets ruined is fourteen. So ask yourself again. Who is the real cheater?
lines.caption: A grown man spends twenty-two thousand dollars to win a children's race. A car company uses children to sell cars and leaves when the bill comes. And the only one whose name gets ruined is fourteen. So ask yourself again. Who is the real cheater?
lines.visual: card:Who is the real cheater?|Akron, Ohio, 1973

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: The Derby still runs every summer, right here. The kids still build the cars. Mostly.
lines.caption: The Derby still runs every summer, right here. The kids still build the cars. Mostly.

lines.speaker: M
lines.say: Akron, Ohio. Keep it real.
lines.caption: Akron, Ohio. Keep it real.
